title: SQA National 5 English — Portfolio–writing (X824/75/03): one piece, marked out of 15, doubled to 30

authority.sitting: Version 3.0, current as downloaded from sqa.org.uk 2026-09-13 (https://www.sqa.org.uk/files_ccc/n5-cat-english.pdf)
authority.why_this_source: SQA's own assessment task document, which states the tariff and the doubling rule in one place. NOT on the drive — fetched from the board's website and saved under protocols/sqa/_sources/ so provenance is on disk (port brief §6).
authority.second_document_read: protocols/sqa/_sources/n5-course-spec-english.pdf (National 5 English Course Specification, Version 6.0, https://www.sqa.org.uk/files_ccc/n5-course-spec-english.pdf) — carries the General marking principles, the Detailed marking instructions and the two band grids (broadly creative, broadly discursive). The assessment-task document says explicitly: 'The marking instructions for the National 5 English portfolio–writing and performance–spoken language can be found in the course specification.'
authority.recurring_pattern_vs_one_series_feature: The portfolio is CENTRE-SET coursework externally marked, so there is no series of past papers to compare. Two documents were read instead (task + specification) and they agree on 30 marks / one piece / out of 15 / doubled / 1,000 words. ⚠️ ONE PIECE is the CURRENT requirement — older National 5 practice (and much third-party revision material) describes TWO pieces at 15 each; do not re-derive the two-piece model from memory.
authority.known_gap: No past-paper exemplars or SQA-published candidate evidence for the portfolio were obtainable at this URL set, so the protocol has no board exemplar to point at. See GOLD MISSING in the port report.

total.why: 'The portfolio–writing is worth 30 marks. It consists of one piece, which is marked out of 15. This is then doubled to give a mark out of 30. This is 30% of the overall marks for the course assessment.'

questions.type: one piece of writing — broadly creative OR broadly discursive; HOLISTIC, level-based, best-fit
questions.ao_note: SQA National 5 English has NO numbered assessment objectives. The specification's marking strands are CONTENT and STYLE, judged holistically.
questions.formula: Judge the piece holistically on CONTENT and STYLE against the grid for the chosen genre. Bands: 15–13 / 12–10 / 9–7 / 6–4 / 3–1. Satisfactory technical accuracy is a REQUIREMENT for the 9–7 band, so a piece whose meaning is not clear at first reading cannot reach 7. Best-fit rule: evidence almost matching the band above → highest mark in the range; work just meeting the described standard → lowest mark in the range; otherwise the middle. The mark out of 15 is then doubled.
questions.quote: This is then doubled to give a mark out of 30
questions.marks_note: The 15 is quoted separately: 'It consists of one piece, which is marked out of 15' and 'You can gain up to 15 marks for the piece of writing. Your mark will be doubled to achieve the 30% weighting.'
questions.volume_rule: 'The written text produced by the candidates must be of no more than 1,000 words, but full marks can be achieved in a shorter piece, if appropriate to purpose (for example poetry). There is no minimum word count. If the word count exceeds the maximum by more than 10%, a penalty will be applied.' (course specification, Version 6.0). ⚠️ SQA's word rule is a CEILING ON LENGTH, the opposite direction to AQA's under-length ceiling: there is NO under-length penalty at all, and the penalty fires only ABOVE 1,100 words.
questions.why: Both documents state 30 marks for the portfolio and 15 for the piece; the doubling is the board's own arithmetic, quoted.
